aztec-nr - noir_aztec::state_vars

Module state_vars

Storage for contract state.

Contracts store their state in state variables. In Solidity, a state variable is simply any value declared inside a contract, e.g. contract Token { uint256 totalSupply; }, and they can be one of many kinds (primitive values, mappings, arrays, immutable, etc.).

Due to Aztec contracts being able to store both public and private state, there are many more different types of state variables, each with their nuance and use cases. Understanding these is key to understanding how a contract works.

Structs

  • DelayedPublicMutable
    Public mutable values with private read access.
  • Map
    A key-value container for state variables.
  • Owned
    Per-account state variable.
  • PrivateImmutable
    Per-account immutable private state.
  • PrivateMutable
    Per-account mutable private state.
  • PrivateSet
    Per-account aggregated private state.
  • PublicImmutable
    Immutable public values.
  • PublicMutable
    Mutable public values.
  • SinglePrivateImmutable
    Contract-wide immutable private state.
  • SinglePrivateMutable
    Contract-wide mutable private state.
  • SingleUseClaim
    Private right to perform an action.
  • Storable
    Exported storage layout definition.

Traits

  • OwnedStateVariable
    A trait that defines the interface for Aztec state variables that have an owner. Unlike regular state variables, owned state variables need to be wrapped in Owned state variable when placed in storage:
  • StateVariable
    A trait that defines the common interface for all Aztec state variables. State variables are variables that can be stored in the contract's storage. Examples of state variables are Owned, PublicMutable, Map or DelayedPublicMutable.
